entries.what: Universal Analytics hits sent directly to google-analytics.com/collect or /batch with v=1 and tid=UA-... Google's sunset page names the product, not these endpoints; tying them to Universal Analytics is a reading from DEAD-APIS.md, backed by the old protocol docs now redirecting to the sunset page. Google's support page (https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11583528) says standard Universal Analytics properties stopped processing hits starting July 1, 2023, and access to the interface, API and data ended starting July 1, 2024, so a standard property's hits stopped counting a year before diedOn.

source.quote: no longer available as of July 1, 2024

lookFor: Requests to google-analytics.com/collect or google-analytics.com/batch, on any subdomain such as www or ssl

The hit parameter tid=UA-... in a query string or form body. v=1 alone isn't matched, since a cache-buster like style.css?v=1 looks the same, and neither is an object shaped like { v: 1, tid: ... } or a tid built from a variable: those are found through the host URL, so read the code around that hit
Not /g/collect or /mp/collect, and not tid=G-...: those are GA4 and still live

A bare /collect or /batch built onto a host held elsewhere, as in GA + '/collect'. It has the shape of an app's own route, so it needs reading. /debug/collect is the same protocol's validation endpoint
entries.replacement: The sunset page only says to get started with Google Analytics. For server hits and Manifest V3 Chrome extensions, Google's GA4 pages give the Measurement Protocol: POST https://www.google-analytics.com/mp/collect?measurement_id=G-XXXX&api_secret=SECRET with a JSON body holding client_id and events: [{name, params}]. For code running in a web page, they say to use the Google tag (gtag.js) or Google Tag Manager instead. Pages: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/collection/protocol/ga4/sending-events and https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/gtagjs.
requires: Read the GA4 measurement ID and API secret from config, and say in the PR what a person must set: nobody has these yet, and they can't be derived from the UA- ID.

A person creates the secret in Google Analytics under Admin > Data collection and modification > Data streams > the stream > Measurement Protocol API secrets, and copies the measurement ID (usually starting G-) from Stream details.
The api_secret is private: Google says not to expose it in client-side code, so never put it in browser code; a hit sent from a web page moves to gtag.js or through the app's own server.
Manifest V3 Chrome extensions can't load gtag.js, so Google recommends the Measurement Protocol there even though the secret ships inside the extension: say this exposure in the PR.
Only HTTP POST with a JSON body works: a GET, an image pixel or a form-encoded v=1 body has to be rewritten.

client_id is required in the body and should match the ID the Google tag generated; an extension keeps its own in browser.storage.local, which needs the storage permission. UA's cid carrying this value is a reading, not on a live Google page.
Each hit becomes an event with a name and params. A /batch call becomes one body with at most 25 events, each with at most 25 parameters, under 130kB.
Event and parameter names must be 40 characters or fewer, use only letters, numbers and underscores, and start with a letter. Event names are case sensitive.
Reserved names can't be used, such as session_start, first_visit, user_engagement and error; parameter names can't begin with _, firebase_, ga_, google_ or gtag.
Web streams use page_view, not screen_view: a UA pageview or screenview hit maps to page_view (the UA side of that mapping is a reading).

Move custom dimensions such as cd1 into named event params. Each must also be registered in Admin > Custom definitions, a step for a person, or the data is collected but isn't available in reports. The cd1-to-name mapping can't be derived, so read what each one means from the code.
Parameter values must be 100 characters or fewer on a standard property, so old long values may need trimming.

Add session_id and engagement_time_msec to event params, or user activity won't show in reports like Realtime. Measurement Protocol alone may give only partial reporting, and hits lose information such as geolocation.
The endpoint returns no HTTP error codes even for a malformed event, so a success check proves nothing: validate against /debug/mp/collect, which returns validationMessages.

entries.what: Universal Analytics on web pages: the analytics.js library and its ga('create', ...) and ga('send', ...) commands. Google's support page (https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11583528) says standard Universal Analytics properties stopped processing hits starting July 1, 2023, and access to the interface, API and data ended starting July 1, 2024, so a standard property's hits stopped counting a year before diedOn.
lookFor: A script loaded from google-analytics.com/analytics.js (a repo's own file that happens to be called analytics.js doesn't count)
ga('create', ...) and ga('send', ...) calls, in either quote style, including on window.ga. Not ReactGA.ga(...) from react-ga4, which is alive, or a name that ends in ga, such as saga(...)
entries.replacement: The sunset page only says to get started with Google Analytics. For web pages, Google's GA4 pages give the Google tag (gtag.js): load https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=TAG_ID, call gtag('config', 'G-XXXX'), and send events with gtag('event', name, params). Page: https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/gtagjs.
requires: Read the G- measurement ID from config, and say in the PR what a person must set: nobody has one yet, and it can't be derived from the UA- ID. It's in Google Analytics under Admin > Data collection and modification > Data streams > the web stream.
No API secret belongs in this code: gtag.js doesn't use one, and the Measurement Protocol secret must never reach client-side code.

A manual pageview on route change must be deleted. On a single-page site the Google tag also sends page_view on history changes, even with send_page_view: false, so turn off "Page changes based on browser history events" in the stream's Enhanced Measurement settings if the code keeps its own pageview. Otherwise pageviews count twice.

ga('send', 'event', category, action, label, value) becomes gtag('event', name, params): choose one event name and carry the rest as params. The old argument shape is a reading, not on a live Google page.
Event names must start with a letter, use only letters, numbers and underscores, are case sensitive, and can't be reserved names such as session_start or first_visit.

Move custom dimensions (ga('set', 'dimension1', ...) or cd1) into named event params. Each must also be registered in Admin > Custom definitions, a step for a person, or the data isn't available in reports. Parameter names can't begin with _, firebase_, ga_, google_ or gtag.

If the site sends a Content-Security-Policy, Google's list for Analytics without Ads features allows https://www.googletagmanager.com in script-src-elem, https://www.googletagmanager.com and https://*.google-analytics.com in img-src, and those two plus https://*.google.com in connect-src. With Ads features on, Google's default list needs more hosts, so read https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/guides/csp.

entries.what: Universal Analytics property IDs, which start UA-. Matching the UA-digits-digits shape is a reading: the sunset page doesn't describe the ID format. Google's support page (https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11583528) says standard Universal Analytics properties stopped processing hits starting July 1, 2023, and access to the interface, API and data ended starting July 1, 2024, so a standard property's hits stopped counting a year before diedOn.

source.quote: no longer available as of July 1, 2024

lookFor: Property IDs shaped like UA-12345678-1: UA-, at least four digits, a hyphen, then digits, in code, config, env examples or HTML. Case sensitive and digits only, so ua-parser-js, X-UA-Compatible and Sec-CH-UA-Platform-Version don't count
entries.replacement: A GA4 measurement ID, which Google says usually starts with G-, used with the Google tag (gtag.js) on web pages or as measurement_id on the Measurement Protocol's /mp/collect. Pages: https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9539598 and https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/collection/protocol/ga4/sending-events.
requires: Read the measurement ID from config, and say in the PR what a person must set: it can't be derived from the UA- ID, so never make one up. It's in Google Analytics under Admin > Data collection and modification > Data streams > the web stream.
Changing the ID isn't enough on its own: whatever sends the data (analytics.js, /collect hits or a library) has to move as well, since a G- ID doesn't work there. That last part is a reading.

entries.what: The npm package react-ga, a library built on Universal Analytics. Google's page doesn't name it: this comes from DEAD-APIS.md and is a reading. react-ga4 is a different package and doesn't count. Google's support page (https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11583528) says standard Universal Analytics properties stopped processing hits starting July 1, 2023, and access to the interface, API and data ended starting July 1, 2024, so a standard property's hits stopped counting a year before diedOn.
lookFor: react-ga as a dependency or import (not react-ga4)
entries.replacement: The Google tag (gtag.js) with a G- measurement ID, which is what Google's GA4 pages give for web pages. Google's pages don't name a React wrapper, so any wrapper package is the fix session's own choice and should be said in the PR. Page: https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/gtagjs.
requires: Read the G- measurement ID from config, and say in the PR what a person must set: nobody has one yet, and it can't be derived from the UA- ID.
Remove the react-ga dependency, not just its imports.

A manual pageview on route change must be deleted. On a single-page site the Google tag also sends page_view on history changes, even with send_page_view: false, so turn off "Page changes based on browser history events" in the stream's Enhanced Measurement settings if the code keeps its own pageview. Otherwise pageviews count twice.
Category and action style events become one event name plus params. That the old call has this shape is a reading from react-ga, not on a Google page.
Event names must start with a letter, use only letters, numbers and underscores, are case sensitive, and can't be reserved names.
Move custom dimensions into named event params, and tell a person to register each one in Admin > Custom definitions, or the data isn't available in reports.

entries.what: The npm package universal-analytics, a server-side library that sends Universal Analytics hits. Google's page doesn't name it: this comes from DEAD-APIS.md and is a reading. Google's support page (https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11583528) says standard Universal Analytics properties stopped processing hits starting July 1, 2023, and access to the interface, API and data ended starting July 1, 2024, so a standard property's hits stopped counting a year before diedOn.
lookFor: universal-analytics as a dependency or import
entries.replacement: The Measurement Protocol, which Google's GA4 pages give for server-side use: POST https://www.google-analytics.com/mp/collect?measurement_id=G-XXXX&api_secret=SECRET with a JSON body holding client_id and events: [{name, params}]. Google's pages don't name a package for this, and a plain fetch works. Page: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/collection/protocol/ga4/sending-events.
requires: Read the GA4 measurement ID and API secret from config, and say in the PR what a person must set: nobody has these yet. The secret is under Admin > Data collection and modification > Data streams > the stream > Measurement Protocol API secrets.
The api_secret is private: keep it in server config, and never send it to client-side code or commit it.
client_id is required in the body and should match the ID the Google tag generated, if the site has one.
Each hit becomes an event with a name and params, at most 25 events to a request and 25 parameters to an event.
Event and parameter names must be 40 characters or fewer, use only letters, numbers and underscores, and start with a letter. Reserved names can't be used.
Move custom dimensions such as cd1 into named event params, and tell a person to register each one in Admin > Custom definitions, or the data isn't available in reports.
Add session_id and engagement_time_msec to event params, or activity won't show in reports like Realtime.
The endpoint returns no HTTP error codes even for a malformed event, so validate against /debug/mp/collect.
Sending events only through the Measurement Protocol may give partial reporting: Google says to use it alongside tagging (gtag, Tag Manager or Firebase).
